findings.text: vdpa config operations form a callback table in three groups. Queue management covers address programming, count programming, kick with and without payload, callback install, ready set and query, state save and restore, vendor statistics, notification area query, interrupt query and size query. Device handling covers alignment, group assignment, descriptor group, feature discovery and negotiation, config change callback, queue count bounds, identifiers, status access, reset variants, suspend and resume, config space sizing and access, generation, address range and affinity. Mapping handling covers whole table install, single entry add and remove, map reset, group to address space binding, queue map query and memory context bind and unbind, plus a final release hook.
Compatible reset clean map flag has numeric value one and selects clearing of existing mappings during reset.

vdpa device allocation helper sizes an enclosing driver structure with compile time offset validation, forwards parent, config, map, group count, address space count, name and address mode to an underlying allocator, then recovers the enclosing object from its embedded generic member.
vdpa driver combines a generic device driver with a probe entry receiving a vdpa device and a remove entry releasing it.
vdpa driver registration associates the registering driver with the current module owner.
vdpa driver module helper wires module load to registration and module unload to unregistration.
Driver and device conversions recover the enclosing vdpa driver from an embedded generic driver and the enclosing vdpa device from an embedded generic device.
Driver data helpers get and set a private pointer through the embedded device, and a map helper returns the cached virtio address map stored in the device.

vdpa reset holds the device configuration lock for writing, marks negotiated features invalid, prefers the compatible reset operation when a nonzero flag word is supplied and that operation exists and otherwise uses plain reset, then releases the lock and returns the result.
vdpa feature programming holds the same configuration lock for writing in the outer helper and delegates to an unlocked helper that marks features valid before invoking the driver feature operation.
vdpa management operations define addition of a named device with creation config, removal of an existing device, and attribute update from a config object.

vdpa management device holds a parent device pointer, management operations pointer, virtio identifier table, mask of settable config attributes, list linkage, supported feature mask and ceiling on supported queue count.
vdso data page setup is an empty inline with no observable effect in this configuration.
Secondary and platform keyring selectors are small sentinel pointer values one and two respectively.
System keyring identifier check accepts only values up to the platform sentinel and rejects larger values as invalid argument.
Key use enumeration identifies verification purposes for module, firmware, kexec PE, key signature, key self signature, unspecified and BPF, terminated by a count marker.
Module magic string is composed from release plus SMP token, preempt token, unload token, modversions token, architecture token and randstruct token in that order.

Magic option tokens vary by configuration: SMP present or empty, preempt real time versus plain preempt versus empty, unload present or empty, modversions present or empty, and randstruct with hashed seed suffix or empty.
vfio device set groups related devices by an opaque set identifier, a mutex, a device list and a device count.

vfio device carries public state including physical device pointer, device operations, migration and logging operations, optional group linkage, set membership, migration flags, precopy version and KVM pointer, plus private lifecycle state including index, embedded device object, optional character device, reference and open counts, completion, iommufd handles, KVM release hook, inode, PASID allocator and attach flags, opened and no-iommu bits and debug directory. Some members exist only under specific build options.

vfio device operations form a driver table for init and release, iommufd bind and unbind, address space attach and detach including PASID variants, device open and close, read, write, ioctl, region capability reporting, mmap, release notification, string and token UUID matching, DMA unmap notification and generic feature handling with flags and user buffer.
In this configuration iommufd helpers report no context and device identifier as not owned, and physical plus emulated bind, unbind, attach and detach operations are null.
vfio character device opened helper reports the stored opened flag.
vfio migration operations define transition to a new state returning a stream object, query of current state and query of stop copy size.
vfio logging operations define dirty tracking start over a cached interval tree with node count and page size output, stop, and read and clear over an address range into a bitmap.

vfio feature validation rejects unsupported get or set bits, accepts probe alone without further checks, otherwise requires at least one of get or set and requires the supplied size to meet a minimum, reporting success with a positive return.

vfio precopy ioctl validation accepts only the get precopy info command, copies a fixed leading prefix from user space, requires reported size to cover that prefix, preserves legacy flag behavior but clears flags for version two devices, and reports inappropriate ioctl, fault or invalid size on failure.

vfio device allocation sizes an enclosing driver structure with offset validation, forwards size, parent device and operations to an underlying allocator and recovers the enclosing object, while put releases a reference through the embedded device object.
File role helpers in this configuration always report that a file is not a group file and does not hold a given device.
Maximum pinned page entries equals how many unsigned long values fit in one page.
vfio info capability pairs a capability buffer header with its total size.

virqfd describes event driven injection with opaque token, event context, handler and thread callbacks plus callback data, work items for injection, shutdown and flush, a wait queue entry, a poll table and a back pointer to the registration slot.

VFS debug checks have two build modes. Enabled mode maps plain checks to faulting and warning primitives, with inode variants dumping the inode before faulting or warning and warn once and plain warn forwarding formatted messages. Disabled mode reduces all of them to compile time expression validity checks, with inode bug mapping to the plain bug form.

vhost translation entry holds a tree node plus list link, an inclusive address interval with size, a translated address, permission bits, padding, a subtree maximum hint and an opaque cookie. The table aggregates entries in a cached tree plus list with a limit, a count and flags.
vhost map permissions use one for read, two for write and three for both, and the retire flag uses one.

VM event zone helpers expand either to a per zone enumerator built from a supplied stem plus a zone suffix or to nothing, depending on whether the zone is configured. Covered zones are DMA, DMA32, high memory and device.

vdpa probe and remove serve as driver bind and unbind entries, while management add, delete and attribute change serve as device lifecycle entries invoked with a management device and optional name or config.

vfio open, close, read, write, ioctl, mmap and release request serve as user facing device entries, while migration state transition and queries plus log start, stop and read and clear serve as migration and tracking entries.
Virtqueue interrupt assignment must not change once DRIVER_OK status is set.
vfio migration, logging and debug properties are static and must be assigned before device registration.
VFS inode bug check faults after dumping state, so it must guard only unreachable conditions.
Header inclusion guards define single markers to prevent repeated inclusion.
